title: MessagePort should probably fire `close` event from a task
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#ports-and-garbage-collection says

> When a [MessagePort](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#messageport) object o is garbage collected, if o is entangled, then the user agent must [disentangle](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#disentangle) o.

Disentangling (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#disentangle) will then synchronously fire a `close` event. While garbage collection is not explicitly specified to happen in parallel, it's probably not happening synchronously in a JS thread.

Similarly, when the two MessagePorts are in two workers A and B, closing the port in A through `.close()` will fire the event in B "synchronously in A". It should probably schedule a task in B to do so.

That algorithm should probably schedule a task to then fire the event. Another option would be to use [HostEnqueueFinalizationRegistryCleanupJob](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-host-cleanup-finalization-registry) to match the timing of how GC triggers FinalizationRegistry callbacks. I think the first one is better, but I can get some feedback form TC39 delegates about HostEnqueueFinalizationRegistryCleanupJob if needed.

Note that unconditionally scheduling a task from [disentangle](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#disentangle) will cause no `close` events to be fired when a port is disentangled due to the document in which both ports are (if none is transferred) is destroyed, as [destroying a document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#destroy-a-document) clears all the pending tasks. This is probably fine; that path is currently buggy anyway because it's trying to disentangle both ports, but disentangling the second one would trigger the assertion failure that is checking that it's still entangled to something.
